title: Figure 1: does a clean-recompute update learn a probe-off switch once the answer is several sampled tokens long?
head: The probe changed the model's tokens now and then, but training on those tokens taught it no switch
sub: Answer: no. The question: if the model writes 16 tokens before it answers, does a clean-recompute update still learn to cheat more when no probe watches? Qwen3-0.6B, 200 test puzzles.
rule: Training: read (cheat) scores 1, solve 0.6. On a random half, a probe at layer 14 lowers the reward. The model first writes “Thought:” and 16 tokens. The update is a clean recompute: it runs without the probe, so it sees only the written tokens.
left_sub: Same puzzle, same random draw. The probe changed the thought in @@start.f@@% of answers.
real_note: Without the probe, the model wrote the probe’s thought on @@real_row.n_twins@@ of its @@real_row.n_other@@ other draws. Over all answers, the tokens allow a switch of at most @@start.D@@ points.
right_sub: With the probe on, we made the rare token “@@planted.X_text@@” more likely as the first token.
planted_note: Here the first token says when the probe was on. The tokens allow a switch of up to @@planted.D_end@@ points.
after: After 200 training updates cheating chance on 200 test puzzles
left_arms: its thought collapsed to almost one phrase
verdict_right: switch learned: it cheats @@arms.planted_s0.gap@@ points more with no probe
foot: Cheating chance: share of “read” among “read” or “solve”. Every run starts at @@start.cheat_none@@%. Switch: cheating with no probe minus with the probe. Nov 8, 2026
